![](images/bekb-geschaeftsbericht-2006/bekb-geschaeftsbericht-2006.pdf-0022-01.png) Client proximity in action, with the mobile banks… ![](images/bekb-geschaeftsbericht-2006/bekb-geschaeftsbericht-2006.pdf-0022-03.png) One of the bank’s major success factors is its proximity and commitment to its customer base of around 500,000 and the fact that it is firmly rooted in the local economy and living environment. The bank offers its customers a complete counseling and customer service program tailored to meet their personal needs. They can contact staff quickly and easily. 123 also expanded its commitments towards families. Around 10,500 people took part in the Family Days in Solothurn and Berne. The concerts given by the Bernese Youth Brass Orchestra were very well received again. Throughout 2006, over 100,000 people were reached at various events. …in 78 meeting centers… ![](images/bekb-geschaeftsbericht-2006/bekb-geschaeftsbericht-2006.pdf-0022-07.png) …and in the Family Days 20 ### **Long-term financial objective** 123 has set itself a long-term financial objective: it aims to achieve free cash flow amounting to CHF 800 million to 1 billion within ten years (from 2003 until 2012). This will entail generating the equivalent of the bank’s target equity, which is some 120 percent of the required equity amount. The cumulative free cash flow of CHF 513.2 million in value added between 2003 and 2006 exceeds the original target. Of the free cash flow that will be achieved by 2012, half will be disbursed to share owners and half will be used for business development purposes. The value added in individual years may vary considerably according to the state of the economy and the amount of investments realized. 123’s primary goal has always been to provide the citizens of the canton of Berne with a robust and sound bank. 123 is committed to the realization of efficient bank governance accompanied by expert oversight so that it can do its part to further the development of the canton of Berne and its infrastructures. 123 bases all of its activities on proximity to its clientele; a broad stockholder and customer base; and the maintenance and development of a work force that is committed to continuity. For continuity is what 123 policies and management are all about, and it intends to continue pursuing this goal in the future. 21 **Ruth, Bruno and Alex Scheidegger (from left to right) have specialized in scaffolding. **Work and orders for companies in the Espace Mittelland** The business year 2006 in brief ### **Dear Stockholders** Your bank again achieved a good result in the past year and has come a further step closer to achieving its ten-year goal. After four years, free cash flow with a total of CHF 513 million is beyond the target range. Annual profit prior to taxes and prior to profit from the partial disposal of a participation increased again in the past year for the fourteenth time in a row. On the basis of 123’s positive result and its solid foundation, we propose the tenth dividend increase in a row from CHF 3.50 to CHF 3.80 as well as a nominal value repayment of CHF 5.00 per registered share. At the last general meeting, we put you, our stockholders, at the center. With a total of 56,000 coowners, the bank is among the first ten Swiss companies in terms of broad public ownership. This establishment in the public with the canton of Berne as its main stockholder forms the basis for a successful development of the bank. Many small and mediumsized companies in the Espace Mittelland that function as suppliers for 123 and regularly execute orders for our bank also benefit from this fact. At this year’s general meeting of stockholders, we will present to you our regular suppliers in the Espace Mittelland. Some of these are contained in the present brochure. 123 contributes to a creation of value and to the strengthening and independent development of our economic environment and living space through this type of business relationship with small and medium-sized companies. ### **Free cash flow exceeds target – Private banking activities expanded – Authorization requested for nominal value repayment and tenth dividend increase** 123 has set itself a long-term financial goal: it aims to achieve free cash flow amounting to CHF 800 million to 1 billion within ten years (from 2003 until 2012). After four years, added value with a total of CHF 513.2 million is beyond the target range. Focusing on two core businesses and governance that aims for a bank with a strong balance sheet structure, robust refinancing, optimized earning power and a stronger equity position have once again proven to be the right strategy. Annual profit prior to taxes and prior to profit from the partial sale of a participation increased again in the past year for the fourteenth time in a row: in 2006 profits were up 4.3 percent to CHF 126.4 million. In addition, the bank registered an extraordinary after-tax profit amounting to CHF 42.5 million resulting from the sale of shares in BKW FMB Energie AG, which was allocated in full to reserves for general banking risks. Annual net profit (after deducting tax expenses amounting to CHF 46.6 million) was CHF 92.2 million, up CHF 7.1 million over the prior year. #### **Free cash flow (FCF) above the target range** Net free cash flow in million francs

As a bank addressing some 100,000 clients each year at events and promotions,** 789 **appreciates the range of services provided by this company in Wabern.** ### **Dividend increase – nominal value repayment** In the first core business, small and mid-sized loans were granted to private individuals, small and medium-sized businesses and business startups in the Espace Mittelland. Home mortgages were up by CHF 417 million and customer assets rose by CHF 482 million. In its second core business, private banking, managed customer assets increased by CHF 1.2 billion to CHF 20.1 billion. On the basis of the bank’s good result and its solid foundation, the tenth dividend increase in a row from CHF 3.50 to CHF 3.80 per share as well as a nominal value repayment of CHF 5.00 per registered share will be proposed to stockholders. #### **Assets under management** in billion francs

### **Robust earning power** 123’s operational income was divided as follows in 2006: profit on interest: 56.2 percent; interest and dividends on financial assets: 6 percent; commissions and services: 21.9 percent; miscellaneous: 15.9 percent. Profit on interest amounted to CHF 278.8 million, a 2-percent increase relative to the prior year. Thanks to the loan policies that the bank has been applying consistently since their inception in 1993, dynamic loan processing and low interest rates, at-risk income again remained at a low level in 2006 (CHF 1.3 million). 123’s proven risk policy has enabled it to reduce the formation of new provisions for loans by CHF 0.4 million to CHF 5.1 million. Its asset management activities constitute its main source of commission and service income. The CHF 96.2 million in commissions the bank earned in 2006 was up 15.2 percent over 2005. The bank’s 2006 profit on commercial transactions (CHF 22.6 million) was on a par with that of the prior year, and was deliberately kept at a low level in accordance with the bank’s governance policies. Operating expenses rose by 1.2 percent to CHF 221.0 million subject to higher personnel expenses. The cost income ratio lay within the target range of 50 to 55 percent. #### **Net pre-tax profit** in million francs

### **8014 new loans** 123 granted 8014 new loans worth a total of CHF 1.5 billion in 2006. Total borrowings (excluding public institutions) increased to CHF 13.9 billion, and total mortgage obligations rose by 3 percent to CHF 13.2 billion. The bank’s loan portfolio remained at the same high quality level as in the previous year. Non-performing loans accounted for less than 1 percent of all loans. The share of individual loans accounted for by mortgages, fixed disbursements and credits worth less than CHF 1 million rose to 89 percent, whereas loans exceeding CHF 30 million accounted for less than 5 percent of all loans. In view of the fact that interest rates increased moderately, more variable interest mortgages were concluded while demand for fixed interest mortgages declined slightly, accounting for 75.1 percent of all mortgages as at the end of 2006 (versus 77.7 percent in 2005). In granting loans, the bank checks to ensure that customers have the financial capability to repay loans even if interest rates stabilize at a higher level. Its provisions for individual and lump sum reimbursements remained unchanged as at the end of the year (4.3 percent of all customer loans). ### **Strong support for SMEs and business startups** 123 placed particular emphasis in 2006 on small and medium-sized loans. It is committed to supporting innovative SMEs and business startups on the basis of a three pronged approach: financing business startups and enterprise growth; succession process financing; and seed financing. 108 projects of this type were financed in 2006 as part of this program, which promoted the creation or preservation of 801 jobs. CHF 100.9 million of the earmarked CHF 150 million for the program had been disbursed by the end of 2006, which means that the bank is still in a position to support business startups and innovative small businesses. It also earmarked additional funds for seed financing. In 2006 the bank increased, from CHF 30 to CHF 50 million, the funds earmarked for established SMEs in the medical technology and biotechnology sectors. 123 supported startups and the development of innovative and competitive SMEs in collaboration with Stiftung für technologische Innovation STI, BioMedinvest AG, BioMedCredit AG, and CGS Management und Beteiligungs AG.
